question.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u=2x+1.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}u=2\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=2x+1$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{6}{\sqrt{(2x+1)^{5}}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{\sqrt{{u}^{5}}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{6}{\sqrt{(2x+1)^{5}}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{u}^{5/2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }3{u}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}3{u}^{-5/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-2{u}^{-3/2}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[{u}^{-3/2}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }[\frac{1}{{a}^{3/2}}-\frac{1}{{1}^{3/2}}] \\  & =-2\cdot (0-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
